passages.text: In the second year of his reign, Nebuchadnezzar had dreams that troubled his spirit, and sleep escaped him.
passages.sermon:
Nebuchadnezzar was king.
He ruled for two years.
In the second year, Nebuchadnezzar had dreams.
These dreams troubled his spirit.
He could not sleep.
passages.original: וּבִשְׁנַ֣ת שְׁתַּ֗יִם לְמַלְכוּת֙ נְבֻֽכַדְנֶצַּ֔ר חָלַ֥ם נְבֻֽכַדְנֶצַּ֖ר חֲלֹמ֑וֹת וַתִּתְפָּ֣עֶם רוּח֔וֹ וּשְׁנָת֖וֹ נִהְיְתָ֥ה עָלָֽיו׃

passages.text: So the king gave orders to summon the magicians, enchanters, sorcerers, and astrologers to explain his dreams. When they came and stood before the king, he said to them, “I have had a dream, and my spirit is anxious to understand it.”
passages.sermon:
King Nebuchadnezzar ruled Babylon.
He had troubling dreams.
He wanted to understand these dreams.
King Nebuchadnezzar gave an order.
He told his servants to summon the magicians.
He told them to bring the enchanters.
He told them to bring the sorcerers.
He told them to bring the astrologers.
He wanted these wise men to explain his dreams.
The magicians, enchanters, sorcerers, and astrologers came.
They stood before King Nebuchadnezzar.
The king spoke to them.
He said, “I have had a dream.”
He said, “My spirit is troubled.”
He said, “I want to know the meaning of the dream.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר הַ֠מֶּלֶךְ לִקְרֹ֨א לַֽחַרְטֻמִּ֜ים וְלָֽאַשָּׁפִ֗ים וְלַֽמְכַשְּׁפִים֙ וְלַכַּשְׂדִּ֔ים לְהַגִּ֥יד לַמֶּ֖לֶךְ חֲלֹמֹתָ֑יו וַיָּבֹ֕אוּ וַיַּֽעַמְד֖וּ לִפְנֵ֥י הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃ וַיֹּ֧אמֶר לָהֶ֛ם הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ חֲל֣וֹם חָלָ֑מְתִּי וַתִּפָּ֣עֶם רוּחִ֔י לָדַ֖עַת אֶֽת־ הַחֲלֽוֹם׃

passages.text: Then the astrologers answered the king in Aramaic, “O king, may you live forever! Tell your servants the dream, and we will give the interpretation.”
passages.sermon:
The astrologers spoke to King Nebuchadnezzar.
They spoke in the Aramaic language.
They said, “O king, may you live forever.
Tell your servants the dream.
We will give you the interpretation.”
passages.original: וַֽיְדַבְּר֧וּ הַכַּשְׂדִּ֛ים לַמֶּ֖לֶךְ אֲרָמִ֑ית מַלְכָּא֙ לְעָלְמִ֣ין חֱיִ֔י אֱמַ֥ר חֶלְמָ֛א לְעַבְדַּיִךְ וּפִשְׁרָ֥א נְחַוֵּֽא׃

passages.text: The king replied to the astrologers, “My word is final: If you do not tell me the dream and its interpretation, you will be cut into pieces and your houses will be reduced to rubble.
passages.sermon:
The king spoke to the astrologers.
He said, “My decision is final.
If you do not tell me the dream,
and if you do not tell me its meaning,
I will have you cut into pieces.
I will destroy your houses.
Your houses will become ruins.”
passages.original: עָנֵ֤ה מַלְכָּא֙ וְאָמַ֣ר לְכַשְׂדָּיֵא מִלְּתָ֖א מִנִּ֣י אַזְדָּ֑א הֵ֣ן לָ֤א תְהֽוֹדְעוּנַּ֙נִי֙ חֶלְמָ֣א וּפִשְׁרֵ֔הּ הַדָּמִין֙ תִּתְעַבְד֔וּן וּבָתֵּיכ֖וֹן נְוָלִ֥י יִתְּשָׂמֽוּן׃

passages.text: But if you tell me the dream and its interpretation, you will receive from me gifts and rewards and great honor. So tell me the dream and its interpretation.”
passages.sermon:
The king of Babylon spoke to the astrologers.
The king said, "If you tell me my dream and its meaning, I will reward you."
I will give you gifts.
I will give you rewards.
I will give you great honor.
Tell me the dream and its meaning."
passages.original: וְהֵ֨ן חֶלְמָ֤א וּפִשְׁרֵהּ֙ תְּֽהַחֲוֺ֔ן מַתְּנָ֤ן וּנְבִזְבָּה֙ וִיקָ֣ר שַׂגִּ֔יא תְּקַבְּל֖וּן מִן־ קֳדָמָ֑י לָהֵ֕ן חֶלְמָ֥א וּפִשְׁרֵ֖הּ הַחֲוֺֽנִי׃

passages.text: They answered a second time, “Let the king tell the dream to his servants, and we will give the interpretation.”
passages.sermon: The astrologers spoke to the king again.\r\nThey said, “King, tell your servants the dream.\r\nWe will give you the interpretation.”
passages.original: עֲנ֥וֹ תִנְיָנ֖וּת וְאָמְרִ֑ין מַלְכָּ֕א חֶלְמָ֛א יֵאמַ֥ר לְעַבְד֖וֹהִי וּפִשְׁרָ֥ה נְהַחֲוֵֽה׃

passages.text: The king replied, “I know for sure that you are stalling for time, because you see that my word is final.
passages.sermon:
The king spoke.
The king replied to his advisors.
The king said, “I know what you are doing.
You are stalling for time.
You delay because you see my word is final.
You know I will not change my decision.
You hope to avoid my command by waiting.
But I see your actions clearly.”
passages.original: עָנֵ֤ה מַלְכָּא֙ וְאָמַ֔ר מִן־ יַצִּיב֙ יָדַ֣ע אֲנָ֔ה דִּ֥י עִדָּנָ֖א אַנְתּ֣וּן זָבְנִ֑ין כָּל־ קֳבֵל֙ דִּ֣י חֲזֵית֔וֹן דִּ֥י אַזְדָּ֖א מִנִּ֥י מִלְּתָֽא׃

passages.text: If you do not tell me the dream, there is only one decree for you. You have conspired to speak before me false and fraudulent words, hoping the situation will change. Therefore tell me the dream, and I will know that you can give me its interpretation.”
passages.sermon:
King Nebuchadnezzar spoke to the wise men of Babylon.
He said, "If you do not tell me the dream, there is only one law for you."
"You have agreed together to speak false and corrupt words before me."
"You hope that the situation will change."
"Therefore, tell me the dream."
"Then I will know that you can show me its interpretation."
passages.original: דִּ֣י הֵן־ חֶלְמָא֩ לָ֨א תְהֽוֹדְעֻנַּ֜נִי חֲדָה־ הִ֣יא דָֽתְכ֗וֹן וּמִלָּ֨ה כִדְבָ֤ה וּשְׁחִיתָה֙ הַזְמִנְתּוּן לְמֵאמַ֣ר קָֽדָמַ֔י עַ֛ד דִּ֥י עִדָּנָ֖א יִשְׁתַּנֵּ֑א לָהֵ֗ן חֶלְמָא֙ אֱמַ֣רוּ לִ֔י וְֽאִנְדַּ֕ע דִּ֥י פִשְׁרֵ֖הּ תְּהַחֲוֻנַּֽנִי׃

passages.text: The astrologers answered the king, “No one on earth can do what the king requests! No king, however great and powerful, has ever asked anything like this of any magician, enchanter, or astrologer.
passages.sermon:
The astrologers stood before the king.
They answered the king.
They said, “No person on earth can do what the king asks.
No king has ever asked such a thing.
No king, no matter how great or powerful, has made this request.
No magician has been asked this.
No enchanter has been asked this.
No astrologer has been asked this.”
passages.original: עֲנ֨וֹ כַשְׂדָּיֵא קֳדָם־ מַלְכָּא֙ וְאָ֣מְרִ֔ין לָֽא־ אִיתַ֤י אֲנָשׁ֙ עַל־ יַבֶּשְׁתָּ֔א דִּ֚י מִלַּ֣ת מַלְכָּ֔א יוּכַ֖ל לְהַחֲוָיָ֑ה כָּל־ קֳבֵ֗ל דִּ֚י כָּל־ מֶ֙לֶךְ֙ רַ֣ב וְשַׁלִּ֔יט מִלָּ֤ה כִדְנָה֙ לָ֣א שְׁאֵ֔ל לְכָל־ חַרְטֹּ֖ם וְאָשַׁ֥ף וְכַשְׂדָּֽי׃

passages.text: What the king requests is so difficult that no one can tell it to him except the gods, whose dwelling is not with mortals.”
passages.sermon:
The king asked for something very difficult.
No one else can answer the king’s request.
Only the gods can reveal this matter.
The gods do not live among people.
passages.original: וּמִלְּתָ֨א דִֽי־ מַלְכָּ֤ה שָׁאֵל֙ יַקִּירָ֔ה וְאָחֳרָן֙ לָ֣א אִיתַ֔י דִּ֥י יְחַוִּנַּ֖הּ קֳדָ֣ם מַלְכָּ֑א לָהֵ֣ן אֱלָהִ֔ין דִּ֚י מְדָ֣רְה֔וֹן עִם־ בִּשְׂרָ֖א לָ֥א אִיתֽוֹהִי׃

passages.text: This response made the king so furious with anger that he gave orders to destroy all the wise men of Babylon.
passages.sermon:
The king heard the astrologers’ answer.
The king became very angry.
The king’s anger was great.
The king gave a command.
He ordered all the wise men in Babylon to be killed.
passages.original: כָּל־ קֳבֵ֣ל דְּנָ֔ה מַלְכָּ֕א בְּנַ֖ס וּקְצַ֣ף שַׂגִּ֑יא וַאֲמַר֙ לְה֣וֹבָדָ֔ה לְכֹ֖ל חַכִּימֵ֥י בָבֶֽל׃

passages.text: So the decree went out that the wise men were to be executed, and men went to look for Daniel and his friends to execute them.
passages.sermon:
King Nebuchadnezzar ruled Babylon.
He became very angry.
He ordered all the wise men of Babylon to be killed.
The king’s officials sent out the decree.
The wise men faced execution.
The officials searched for Daniel and his friends.
They wanted to execute Daniel and his friends too.
passages.original: וְדָתָ֣א נֶפְקַ֔ת וְחַכִּֽימַיָּ֖א מִֽתְקַטְּלִ֑ין וּבְע֛וֹ דָּנִיֵּ֥אל וְחַבְר֖וֹהִי לְהִתְקְטָלָֽה׃פ

passages.text: When Arioch, the commander of the king’s guard, had gone out to execute the wise men of Babylon, Daniel replied with discretion and tact.
passages.sermon:
Arioch was the commander of the king’s guard.
The king ordered Arioch to kill all the wise men of Babylon.
Arioch went out to carry out this order.
Daniel saw what was happening.
Daniel spoke to Arioch.
Daniel used wisdom and good judgment when he spoke.
passages.original: בֵּאדַ֣יִן דָּנִיֵּ֗אל הֲתִיב֙ עֵטָ֣א וּטְעֵ֔ם לְאַרְי֕וֹךְ רַב־ טַבָּחַיָּ֖א דִּ֣י מַלְכָּ֑א דִּ֚י נְפַ֣ק לְקַטָּלָ֔ה לְחַכִּימֵ֖י בָּבֶֽל׃

passages.text: “Why is the decree from the king so harsh?” he asked. At this time Arioch explained the situation to Daniel.
passages.sermon:
Daniel was a wise man in Babylon.
The king of Babylon gave a harsh order.
The king commanded that all the wise men be killed.
Arioch was the commander of the king’s guard.
Arioch went out to carry out the king’s order.
Daniel spoke to Arioch.
Daniel asked Arioch a question.
Daniel said, “Why is the king’s decree so harsh?”
Arioch explained the matter to Daniel.
passages.original: עָנֵ֣ה וְאָמַ֗ר לְאַרְיוֹךְ֙ שַׁלִּיטָ֣א דִֽי־ מַלְכָּ֔א עַל־ מָ֥ה דָתָ֛א מְהַחְצְפָ֖ה מִן־ קֳדָ֣ם מַלְכָּ֑א אֱדַ֣יִן מִלְּתָ֔א הוֹדַ֥ע אַרְי֖וֹךְ לְדָנִיֵּֽאל׃

passages.text: So Daniel went in and asked the king to give him some time, so that he could give him the interpretation.
passages.sermon:
Daniel was a wise man from Judah.
Daniel went to the king of Babylon.
Daniel asked the king for more time.
Daniel wanted time to explain the dream’s meaning to the king.
passages.original: וְדָ֣נִיֵּ֔אל עַ֖ל וּבְעָ֣ה מִן־ מַלְכָּ֑א דִּ֚י זְמָ֣ן יִנְתֵּן־ לֵ֔הּ וּפִשְׁרָ֖א לְהַֽחֲוָיָ֥ה לְמַלְכָּֽא׃פ

passages.text: Then Daniel returned to his house and explained the matter to his friends Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah, urging them to plead for mercy from the God of heaven concerning this mystery, so that Daniel and his friends would not be killed with the rest of the wise men of Babylon.
passages.sermon:
Daniel was a wise man in Babylon.
Daniel returned to his house.
He had three friends.
Their names were Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah.
Daniel explained the matter to his friends.
He told them about the king’s harsh decree.
Daniel urged his friends to pray.
He told them to ask the God of heaven for mercy.
They needed God’s help to reveal the mystery.
Daniel and his friends did not want to die.
The king had ordered all the wise men of Babylon to be killed.
Daniel and his friends were among the wise men.
They prayed so they would not be killed with the others.
passages.original: אֱדַ֥יִן דָּֽנִיֵּ֖אל לְבַיְתֵ֣הּ אֲזַ֑ל וְ֠לַחֲנַנְיָה מִֽישָׁאֵ֧ל וַעֲזַרְיָ֛ה חַבְר֖וֹהִי מִלְּתָ֥א הוֹדַֽע׃ וְרַחֲמִ֗ין לְמִבְעֵא֙ מִן־ קֳדָם֙ אֱלָ֣הּ שְׁמַיָּ֔א עַל־ רָזָ֖ה דְּנָ֑ה דִּ֣י לָ֤א יְהֹֽבְדוּן֙ דָּנִיֵּ֣אל וְחַבְר֔וֹהִי עִם־ שְׁאָ֖ר חַכִּימֵ֥י בָבֶֽל׃

passages.text: During the night, the mystery was revealed to Daniel in a vision, and he blessed the God of heaven and declared: “Blessed be the name of God forever and ever, for wisdom and power belong to Him.
passages.sermon:
Daniel was a wise man in Babylon.
God gave Daniel a vision during the night.
God revealed the mystery to Daniel in this vision.
Daniel blessed the God of heaven.
Daniel spoke and said these words.
He said, “Blessed be the name of God forever and ever.
Wisdom belongs to God.
Power belongs to God.”
passages.original: אֱדַ֗יִן לְדָנִיֵּ֛אל בְּחֶזְוָ֥א דִֽי־ לֵילְיָ֖א רָזָ֣ה גֲלִ֑י אֱדַ֙יִן֙ דָּֽנִיֵּ֔אל בָּרִ֖ךְ לֶאֱלָ֥הּ שְׁמַיָּֽא׃ עָנֵ֤ה דָֽנִיֵּאל֙ וְאָמַ֔ר לֶהֱוֵ֨א שְׁמֵ֤הּ דִּֽי־ אֱלָהָא֙ מְבָרַ֔ךְ מִן־ עָלְמָ֖א וְעַ֣ד־ עָלְמָ֑א דִּ֧י חָכְמְתָ֛א וּגְבוּרְתָ֖א דִּ֥י לֵֽהּ־ הִֽיא׃

passages.text: He changes the times and seasons; He removes kings and establishes them. He gives wisdom to the wise and knowledge to the discerning.
passages.sermon:
God rules over all things.
God changes the times.
God changes the seasons.
God removes kings.
God establishes kings.
God gives wisdom to wise people.
God gives knowledge to people who understand.
passages.original: וְ֠הוּא מְהַשְׁנֵ֤א עִדָּנַיָּא֙ וְזִמְנַיָּ֔א מְהַעְדֵּ֥ה מַלְכִ֖ין וּמְהָקֵ֣ים מַלְכִ֑ין יָהֵ֤ב חָכְמְתָא֙ לְחַכִּימִ֔ין וּמַנְדְּעָ֖א לְיָדְעֵ֥י בִינָֽה׃

passages.text: He reveals the deep and hidden things; He knows what lies in darkness, and light dwells with Him.
passages.sermon:
God reveals deep things.
God reveals hidden things.
God knows what is in darkness.
Light lives with God.
passages.original: ה֛וּא גָּלֵ֥א עַמִּיקָתָ֖א וּמְסַתְּרָתָ֑א יָדַע֙ מָ֣ה בַחֲשׁוֹכָ֔א וּנְהִירָא עִמֵּ֥הּ שְׁרֵֽא׃

passages.text: To You, O God of my fathers, I give thanks and praise, because You have given me wisdom and power. And now You have made known to me what we have requested, for You have made known to us the dream of the king.”
passages.sermon:
Daniel spoke to God.
God is the God of Daniel’s ancestors.
Daniel gave thanks to God.
Daniel praised God.
God gave Daniel wisdom.
God gave Daniel power.
God made known to Daniel what he and his friends had asked.
God revealed the king’s dream to Daniel and his friends.
passages.original: לָ֣ךְ׀ אֱלָ֣הּ אֲבָהָתִ֗י מְהוֹדֵ֤א וּמְשַׁבַּח֙ אֲנָ֔ה דִּ֧י חָכְמְתָ֛א וּגְבוּרְתָ֖א יְהַ֣בְתְּ לִ֑י וּכְעַ֤ן הֽוֹדַעְתַּ֙נִי֙ דִּֽי־ בְעֵ֣ינָא מִנָּ֔ךְ דִּֽי־ מִלַּ֥ת מַלְכָּ֖א הוֹדַעְתֶּֽנָא׃

passages.text: Therefore Daniel went to Arioch, whom the king had appointed to destroy the wise men of Babylon, and said to him, “Do not execute the wise men of Babylon! Bring me before the king, and I will give him the interpretation.”
passages.sermon:
Daniel was a wise man from Judah.
The king of Babylon had appointed Arioch to destroy the wise men of Babylon.
Daniel went to Arioch.
Daniel spoke to Arioch.
Daniel said, “Do not execute the wise men of Babylon.
Bring me before the king.
I will give the king the interpretation.”
passages.original: כָּל־ קֳבֵ֣ל דְּנָ֗ה דָּֽנִיֵּאל֙ עַ֣ל עַל־ אַרְי֔וֹךְ דִּ֚י מַנִּ֣י מַלְכָּ֔א לְהוֹבָדָ֖ה לְחַכִּימֵ֣י בָבֶ֑ל אֲזַ֣ל׀ וְכֵ֣ן אֲמַר־ לֵ֗הּ לְחַכִּימֵ֤י בָבֶל֙ אַל־ תְּהוֹבֵ֔ד הַעֵ֙לְנִי֙ קֳדָ֣ם מַלְכָּ֔א וּפִשְׁרָ֖א לְמַלְכָּ֥א אֲחַוֵּֽא׃ס

passages.text: Arioch hastily brought Daniel before the king and said to him, “I have found a man among the exiles from Judah who will tell the king the interpretation.”
passages.sermon:
Arioch was an official appointed by the king.
The king had ordered Arioch to destroy the wise men of Babylon.
Daniel was one of the exiles from Judah.
Arioch quickly brought Daniel before the king.
Arioch spoke to the king.
Arioch said, “I have found a man among the exiles from Judah.
This man will tell the king the interpretation.”
passages.original: אֱדַ֤יִן אַרְיוֹךְ֙ בְּהִתְבְּהָלָ֔ה הַנְעֵ֥ל לְדָנִיֵּ֖אל קֳדָ֣ם מַלְכָּ֑א וְכֵ֣ן אֲמַר־ לֵ֗הּ דִּֽי־ הַשְׁכַּ֤חַת גְּבַר֙ מִן־ בְּנֵ֤י גָֽלוּתָא֙ דִּ֣י יְה֔וּד דִּ֥י פִשְׁרָ֖א לְמַלְכָּ֥א יְהוֹדַֽע׃

passages.text: The king responded to Daniel, whose name was Belteshazzar, “Are you able to tell me what I saw in the dream, as well as its interpretation?”
passages.sermon:
King Nebuchadnezzar spoke to Daniel.
Daniel was also called Belteshazzar.
The king asked Daniel a question.
He said, “Can you tell me what I saw in my dream?
Can you also tell me what the dream means?”
passages.original: עָנֵ֤ה מַלְכָּא֙ וְאָמַ֣ר לְדָנִיֵּ֔אל דִּ֥י שְׁמֵ֖הּ בֵּלְטְשַׁאצַּ֑ר הַאִיתַיִךְ כָּהֵ֗ל לְהוֹדָעֻתַ֛נִי חֶלְמָ֥א דִֽי־ חֲזֵ֖ית וּפִשְׁרֵֽהּ׃

passages.text: Daniel answered the king, “No wise man, enchanter, medium, or magician can explain to the king the mystery of which he inquires.
passages.sermon:
Daniel stood before the king.
Daniel spoke to the king.
Daniel said, “The mystery you ask about is very great.
No wise man can explain this mystery to you.
No enchanter can explain this mystery to you.
No medium can explain this mystery to you.
No magician can explain this mystery to you.
No one among these people can show the king the answer.”
passages.original: עָנֵ֧ה דָנִיֵּ֛אל קֳדָ֥ם מַלְכָּ֖א וְאָמַ֑ר רָזָה֙ דִּֽי־ מַלְכָּ֣א שָׁאֵ֔ל לָ֧א חַכִּימִ֣ין אָֽשְׁפִ֗ין חַרְטֻמִּין֙ גָּזְרִ֔ין יָכְלִ֖ין לְהַֽחֲוָיָ֥ה לְמַלְכָּֽא׃

passages.text: But there is a God in heaven who reveals mysteries, and He has made known to King Nebuchadnezzar what will happen in the latter days. Your dream and the visions that came into your mind as you lay on your bed were these: As you lay on your bed, O king, your thoughts turned to the future, and the Revealer of Mysteries made known to you what will happen.
passages.sermon:
God lives in heaven.
God reveals mysteries.
God made something known to King Nebuchadnezzar.
God showed the king what will happen in the future.
King Nebuchadnezzar had a dream.
The king saw visions while he lay on his bed.
These dreams and visions came into the king’s mind.
As the king lay on his bed, he thought about the future.
God, who reveals mysteries, showed the king what will happen.
passages.original: בְּרַ֡ם אִיתַ֞י אֱלָ֤הּ בִּשְׁמַיָּא֙ גָּלֵ֣א רָזִ֔ין וְהוֹדַ֗ע לְמַלְכָּא֙ נְבֽוּכַדְנֶצַּ֔ר מָ֛ה דִּ֥י לֶהֱוֵ֖א בְּאַחֲרִ֣ית יוֹמַיָּ֑א חֶלְמָ֨ךְ וְחֶזְוֵ֥י רֵאשָׁ֛ךְ עַֽל־ מִשְׁכְּבָ֖ךְ דְּנָ֥ה הֽוּא׃פ אַ֣נְתְּה מַלְכָּ֗א רַעְיוֹנָךְ֙ עַל־ מִשְׁכְּבָ֣ךְ סְלִ֔קוּ מָ֛ה דִּ֥י לֶהֱוֵ֖א אַחֲרֵ֣י דְנָ֑ה וְגָלֵ֧א רָזַיָּ֛א הוֹדְעָ֖ךְ מָה־ דִ֥י לֶהֱוֵֽא׃

passages.text: And to me this mystery has been revealed, not because I have more wisdom than any man alive, but in order that the interpretation might be made known to the king, and that you may understand the thoughts of your mind.
passages.sermon:
Daniel spoke to King Nebuchadnezzar.
Daniel said God revealed the mystery to him.
Daniel did not receive this mystery because he had more wisdom than any other living person.
God revealed the mystery so the king could know its meaning.
God wanted the king to understand the thoughts in his mind.
passages.original: וַאֲנָ֗ה לָ֤א בְחָכְמָה֙ דִּֽי־ אִיתַ֥י בִּי֙ מִן־ כָּל־ חַיַּיָּ֔א רָזָ֥א דְנָ֖ה גֱּלִ֣י לִ֑י לָהֵ֗ן עַל־ דִּבְרַת֙ דִּ֤י פִשְׁרָא֙ לְמַלְכָּ֣א יְהוֹדְע֔וּן וְרַעְיוֹנֵ֥י לִבְבָ֖ךְ תִּנְדַּֽע׃

passages.text: As you, O king, were watching, a great statue appeared. A great and dazzling statue stood before you, and its form was awesome.
passages.sermon:
King Nebuchadnezzar was watching.
A great statue appeared.
The statue was very large.
The statue was dazzling.
The statue stood in front of the king.
The statue looked awesome and terrifying.
passages.original: אַ֣נְתְּה מַלְכָּ֗א חָזֵ֤ה הֲוַ֙יְתָ֙ וַאֲל֨וּ צְלֵ֥ם חַד֙ שַׂגִּ֔יא צַלְמָ֨א דִּכֵּ֥ן רַ֛ב וְזִיוֵ֥הּ יַתִּ֖יר קָאֵ֣ם לְקָבְלָ֑ךְ וְרֵוֵ֖הּ דְּחִֽיל׃

passages.text: The head of the statue was pure gold, its chest and arms were silver, its belly and thighs were bronze, its legs were iron, and its feet were part iron and part clay.
passages.sermon:
The statue had a head of pure gold.
Its chest and arms were silver.
Its belly and thighs were bronze.
Its legs were iron.
Its feet were partly iron and partly clay.
passages.original: ה֣וּא צַלְמָ֗א רֵאשֵׁהּ֙ דִּֽי־ דְהַ֣ב טָ֔ב חֲד֥וֹהִי וּדְרָע֖וֹהִי דִּ֣י כְסַ֑ף מְע֥וֹהִי וְיַרְכָתֵ֖הּ דִּ֥י נְחָֽשׁ׃ שָׁק֖וֹהִי דִּ֣י פַרְזֶ֑ל רַגְל֕וֹהִי מִנְּהוֹן דִּ֣י פַרְזֶ֔ל וּמִנְּהוֹן דִּ֥י חֲסַֽף׃

passages.text: As you watched, a stone was cut out, but not by human hands. It struck the statue on its feet of iron and clay, and crushed them.
passages.sermon:
The king saw a vision.
He watched a statue.
A stone appeared.
No human cut the stone.
The stone came by itself.
The stone struck the statue.
It hit the statue’s feet.
The feet were made of iron and clay.
The stone crushed the feet.
passages.original: חָזֵ֣ה הֲוַ֗יְתָ עַ֠ד דִּ֣י הִתְגְּזֶ֤רֶת אֶ֙בֶן֙ דִּי־ לָ֣א בִידַ֔יִן וּמְחָ֤ת לְצַלְמָא֙ עַל־ רַגְל֔וֹהִי דִּ֥י פַרְזְלָ֖א וְחַסְפָּ֑א וְהַדֵּ֖קֶת הִמּֽוֹן׃

passages.text: Then the iron, clay, bronze, silver, and gold were shattered and became like chaff on the threshing floor in summer. The wind carried them away, and not a trace of them could be found. But the stone that had struck the statue became a great mountain and filled the whole earth.
passages.sermon:
The iron, clay, bronze, silver, and gold were shattered all at once.
They broke into pieces together.
They became like chaff from the summer threshing floor.
The wind carried them away.
No trace of them could be found anywhere.
The stone struck the statue.
The stone became a great mountain.
The mountain filled the whole earth.
passages.original: בֵּאדַ֣יִן דָּ֣קוּ כַחֲדָ֡ה פַּרְזְלָא֩ חַסְפָּ֨א נְחָשָׁ֜א כַּסְפָּ֣א וְדַהֲבָ֗א וַהֲווֹ֙ כְּע֣וּר מִן־ אִדְּרֵי־ קַ֔יִט וּנְשָׂ֤א הִמּוֹן֙ רוּחָ֔א וְכָל־ אֲתַ֖ר לָא־ הִשְׁתֲּכַ֣ח לְה֑וֹן וְאַבְנָ֣א׀ דִּֽי־ מְחָ֣ת לְצַלְמָ֗א הֲוָ֛ת לְט֥וּר רַ֖ב וּמְלָ֥ת כָּל־ אַרְעָֽא׃

passages.text: This was the dream; now we will tell the king its interpretation.
passages.sermon:
Daniel spoke to King Nebuchadnezzar.
Daniel said, "This was your dream."
Daniel said, "Now we will tell you what it means."
Daniel prepared to explain the meaning to the king.
passages.original: דְּנָ֣ה חֶלְמָ֔א וּפִשְׁרֵ֖הּ נֵאמַ֥ר קֳדָם־ מַלְכָּֽא׃

passages.text: You, O king, are the king of kings, to whom the God of heaven has given sovereignty, power, strength, and glory.
passages.sermon:
You are the king.
You are the king of kings.
The God of heaven has given you your kingdom.
God has given you power.
God has given you strength.
God has given you glory.
passages.original: אַ֣נְתְּה מַלְכָּ֔א מֶ֖לֶךְ מַלְכַיָּ֑א דִּ֚י אֱלָ֣הּ שְׁמַיָּ֔א מַלְכוּתָ֥א חִסְנָ֛א וְתָקְפָּ֥א וִֽיקָרָ֖א יְהַב־ לָֽךְ׃

passages.text: Wherever the sons of men or beasts of the field or birds of the air dwell, He has given them into your hand and has made you ruler over them all. You are that head of gold.
passages.sermon:
God gave you great authority, O king.
God gave you power over all people.
God gave you power over every wild animal.
God gave you power over every bird in the sky.
God put all these under your rule.
You rule over them all.
You are the head of gold.
passages.original: וּבְכָל־ דִּ֣י דָאֲרִין בְּֽנֵי־ אֲ֠נָשָׁא חֵיוַ֨ת בָּרָ֤א וְעוֹף־ שְׁמַיָּא֙ יְהַ֣ב בִּידָ֔ךְ וְהַשְׁלְטָ֖ךְ בְּכָלְּה֑וֹן אַנְתְּה־ ה֔וּא רֵאשָׁ֖ה דִּ֥י דַהֲבָֽא׃

passages.text: But after you, there will arise another kingdom, inferior to yours. Next, a third kingdom, one of bronze, will rule the whole earth.
passages.sermon:
King Nebuchadnezzar, you are the king of kings.
God has given you power and glory.
After you, another kingdom will arise.
This kingdom will be inferior to yours.
Then a third kingdom will come.
This third kingdom will be made of bronze.
It will rule over the whole earth.
passages.original: וּבָתְרָ֗ךְ תְּק֛וּם מַלְכ֥וּ אָחֳרִ֖י אֲרַ֣עא מִנָּ֑ךְ וּמַלְכ֨וּ תְלִיתָיָא אָחֳרִי֙ דִּ֣י נְחָשָׁ֔א דִּ֥י תִשְׁלַ֖ט בְּכָל־ אַרְעָֽא׃

passages.text: Finally, there will be a fourth kingdom as strong as iron; for iron shatters and crushes all things, and like iron that crushes all things, it will shatter and crush all the others.
passages.sermon:
There will be a fourth kingdom.
This kingdom will come after the others.
This fourth kingdom will be very strong.
It will be as strong as iron.
Iron is very hard.
Iron breaks and crushes everything.
This kingdom will act like iron.
It will shatter all the other kingdoms.
It will crush them completely.
passages.original: וּמַלְכוּ֙ רְבִיעָיָה תֶּהֱוֵ֥א תַקִּיפָ֖ה כְּפַרְזְלָ֑א כָּל־ קֳבֵ֗ל דִּ֤י פַרְזְלָא֙ מְהַדֵּ֤ק וְחָשֵׁל֙ כֹּ֔לָּא וּֽכְפַרְזְלָ֛א דִּֽי־ מְרָעַ֥ע כָּל־ אִלֵּ֖ין תַּדִּ֥ק וְתֵרֹֽעַ׃

passages.text: And just as you saw that the feet and toes were made partly of fired clay and partly of iron, so this will be a divided kingdom, yet some of the strength of iron will be in it—just as you saw the iron mixed with clay.
passages.sermon:
The vision showed a statue with feet and toes.
The feet and toes were partly made of fired clay.
The feet and toes were also partly made of iron.
This represents a kingdom.
This kingdom will be divided.
Some parts of the kingdom will be strong like iron.
Other parts will be weak like clay.
The iron and clay were mixed together in the feet and toes.
This means the kingdom will have both strength and weakness.
The strength comes from the iron mixed in.
The weakness comes from the clay mixed in.
passages.original: וְדִֽי־ חֲזַ֜יְתָה רַגְלַיָּ֣א וְאֶצְבְּעָתָ֗א מִנְּהוֹן חֲסַ֤ף דִּֽי־ פֶחָר֙ וּמִנְּהוֹן פַּרְזֶ֔ל מַלְכ֤וּ פְלִיגָה֙ תֶּהֱוֵ֔ה וּמִן־ נִצְבְּתָ֥א דִ֥י פַרְזְלָ֖א לֶֽהֱוֵא־ בַ֑הּ כָּל־ קֳבֵל֙ דִּ֣י חֲזַ֔יְתָה פַּ֨רְזְלָ֔א מְעָרַ֖ב בַּחֲסַ֥ף טִינָֽא׃

passages.text: And as the toes of the feet were partly iron and partly clay, so this kingdom will be partly strong and partly brittle.
passages.sermon:
The toes of the feet were partly iron and partly clay.
This kingdom will be divided.
Part of the kingdom will be strong, like iron.
Part of the kingdom will be brittle, like clay.
passages.original: וְאֶצְבְּעָת֙ רַגְלַיָּ֔א מִנְּהוֹן פַּרְזֶ֖ל וּמִנְּהוֹן חֲסַ֑ף מִן־ קְצָ֤ת מַלְכוּתָא֙ תֶּהֱוֵ֣ה תַקִּיפָ֔ה וּמִנַּ֖הּ תֶּהֱוֵ֥ה תְבִירָֽה׃

passages.text: As you saw the iron mixed with clay, so the peoples will mix with one another, but will not hold together any more than iron mixes with clay.
passages.sermon:
Daniel spoke to King Nebuchadnezzar.
Daniel explained the king’s dream.
Daniel said, “You saw iron mixed with clay.”
Iron and clay do not truly combine.
In the same way, different peoples will mix together.
These peoples will not truly unite.
They will not hold together.
Iron does not mix with clay.
In the same way, these peoples will not become one.”
passages.original: דִי חֲזַ֗יְתָ פַּרְזְלָא֙ מְעָרַב֙ בַּחֲסַ֣ף טִינָ֔א מִתְעָרְבִ֤ין לֶהֱוֺן֙ בִּזְרַ֣ע אֲנָשָׁ֔א וְלָֽא־ לֶהֱוֺ֥ן דָּבְקִ֖ין דְּנָ֣ה עִם־ דְּנָ֑ה הֵֽא־ כְדִ֣י פַרְזְלָ֔א לָ֥א מִתְעָרַ֖ב עִם־ חַסְפָּֽא׃

passages.text: In the days of those kings, the God of heaven will set up a kingdom that will never be destroyed, nor will it be left to another people. It will shatter all these kingdoms and bring them to an end, but will itself stand forever.
passages.sermon:
The God of heaven is powerful and eternal.
He will act during the days of those kings.
He will set up a kingdom.
This kingdom will never be destroyed.
No other people will ever possess this kingdom.
This kingdom will shatter all the other kingdoms.
It will bring all those kingdoms to an end.
This kingdom will stand forever.
passages.original: וּֽבְיוֹמֵיה֞וֹן דִּ֧י מַלְכַיָּ֣א אִנּ֗וּן יְקִים֩ אֱלָ֨הּ שְׁמַיָּ֤א מַלְכוּ֙ דִּ֤י לְעָלְמִין֙ לָ֣א תִתְחַבַּ֔ל וּמַ֨לְכוּתָ֔ה לְעַ֥ם אָחֳרָ֖ן לָ֣א תִשְׁתְּבִ֑ק תַּדִּ֤ק וְתָסֵיף֙ כָּל־ אִלֵּ֣ין מַלְכְוָתָ֔א וְהִ֖יא תְּק֥וּם לְעָלְמַיָּֽא׃

passages.text: And just as you saw a stone being cut out of the mountain without human hands, and it shattered the iron, bronze, clay, silver, and gold, so the great God has told the king what will happen in the future. The dream is true, and its interpretation is trustworthy.”
passages.sermon:
God is great.
God revealed the future to the king.
You saw a stone cut from a mountain.
No human hands cut the stone.
The stone struck the statue.
The stone shattered the iron.
The stone shattered the bronze.
The stone shattered the clay.
The stone shattered the silver.
The stone shattered the gold.
God showed the king what will happen after this.
The dream is true.
The interpretation is trustworthy.
passages.original: כָּל־ קֳבֵ֣ל דִּֽי־ חֲזַ֡יְתָ דִּ֣י מִטּוּרָא֩ אִתְגְּזֶ֨רֶת אֶ֜בֶן דִּי־ לָ֣א בִידַ֗יִן וְ֠הַדֶּקֶת פַּרְזְלָ֨א נְחָשָׁ֤א חַסְפָּא֙ כַּסְפָּ֣א וְדַהֲבָ֔א אֱלָ֥הּ רַב֙ הוֹדַ֣ע לְמַלְכָּ֔א מָ֛ה דִּ֥י לֶהֱוֵ֖א אַחֲרֵ֣י דְנָ֑ה וְיַצִּ֥יב חֶלְמָ֖א וּמְהֵימַ֥ן פִּשְׁרֵֽהּ׃פ

passages.text: At this, King Nebuchadnezzar fell on his face, paid homage to Daniel, and ordered that an offering of incense be presented to him.
passages.sermon:
King Nebuchadnezzar was the ruler of Babylon.
He saw that Daniel had revealed the king’s dream and its meaning.
King Nebuchadnezzar fell on his face before Daniel.
He paid homage to Daniel.
He ordered that an offering and incense be presented to Daniel.
passages.original: בֵּ֠אדַיִן מַלְכָּ֤א נְבֽוּכַדְנֶצַּר֙ נְפַ֣ל עַל־ אַנְפּ֔וֹהִי וּלְדָנִיֵּ֖אל סְגִ֑ד וּמִנְחָה֙ וְנִ֣יחֹחִ֔ין אֲמַ֖ר לְנַסָּ֥כָה לֵֽהּ׃

passages.text: The king said to Daniel, “Your God is truly the God of gods and Lord of kings, the Revealer of Mysteries, since you were able to reveal this mystery.”
passages.sermon:
King Nebuchadnezzar spoke to Daniel.
He said, "Your God is the God of gods.
He is the Lord of kings.
He reveals mysteries.
You were able to reveal this mystery.
This shows that your God truly reveals secrets."
passages.original: עָנֵה֩ מַלְכָּ֨א לְדָנִיֵּ֜אל וְאָמַ֗ר מִן־ קְשֹׁט֙ דִּ֣י אֱלָהֲכ֗וֹן ה֣וּא אֱלָ֧הּ אֱלָהִ֛ין וּמָרֵ֥א מַלְכִ֖ין וְגָלֵ֣ה רָזִ֑ין דִּ֣י יְכֵ֔לְתָּ לְמִגְלֵ֖א רָזָ֥ה דְנָֽה׃

passages.text: Then the king promoted Daniel and gave him many generous gifts. He made him ruler over the entire province of Babylon and chief administrator over all the wise men of Babylon.
passages.sermon:
King Nebuchadnezzar ruled Babylon.
He promoted Daniel.
He gave Daniel many generous gifts.
He made Daniel ruler over the whole province of Babylon.
He made Daniel chief administrator over all the wise men in Babylon.
passages.original: אֱדַ֨יִן מַלְכָּ֜א לְדָנִיֵּ֣אל רַבִּ֗י וּמַתְּנָ֨ן רַבְרְבָ֤ן שַׂגִּיאָן֙ יְהַב־ לֵ֔הּ וְהַ֨שְׁלְטֵ֔הּ עַ֖ל כָּל־ מְדִינַ֣ת בָּבֶ֑ל וְרַב־ סִגְנִ֔ין עַ֖ל כָּל־ חַכִּימֵ֥י בָבֶֽל׃

passages.text: And at Daniel’s request, the king appointed Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego to manage the province of Babylon, while Daniel remained in the king’s court.
passages.sermon:
Daniel was a wise and faithful servant of God.
Daniel asked the king for something.
Daniel requested that Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego be given responsibility.
The king listened to Daniel.
The king appointed Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego to manage the province of Babylon.
Daniel stayed in the king’s court.
passages.original: וְדָנִיֵּאל֙ בְּעָ֣א מִן־ מַלְכָּ֔א וּמַנִּ֗י עַ֤ל עֲבִֽידְתָּא֙ דִּ֚י מְדִינַ֣ת בָּבֶ֔ל לְשַׁדְרַ֥ךְ מֵישַׁ֖ךְ וַעֲבֵ֣ד נְג֑וֹ וְדָנִיֵּ֖אל בִּתְרַ֥ע מַלְכָּֽא׃פ
